claims.text: The opportunity is for individuals from low-income households.
Applicants must not be eligible for tuition fee support from the Scottish Government.
Applicants must be ordinarily resident in Scotland.
Applicants must have completed at least two full years of secondary schooling or college in Scotland, or have a substantial recent connection to Scotland.
Applicants must be entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, or have limited leave to remain, or be asylum seekers.
Applicants must be enrolled on an undergraduate degree course at a Scottish Institute of Higher Education.
The grants cover the cost of tuition fees, up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.
Applicants must demonstrate that their financial circumstances do not allow them to cover the cost of their tuition fees.
Retrospective applications will not be accepted.
Applications will not be accepted if the student has incurred tuition fee debts in a previous year of study and is unable to move to the next level of their course as a result.
The application portal will be open from June 1, 2026, to 5 pm on December 1, 2026.
The opportunity is for undergraduate degree courses in academic year 2026-27.
The grants are designed to help students who do not have the financial resources to attend university.
Applications are considered on a case-by-case basis, taking into account household income and other extenuating circumstances.
In 2025-26, the median household income of award-holders was £10,000 per year.
All applications are made online.
Applicants must complete an eligibility checker before applying.
The result of the eligibility checker is indicative only.
Applicants will receive an automatic reply confirming receipt of their application.

Late applications after the closing date will not be accepted, unless the student can demonstrate that they were first informed that SAAS would not be covering their fees after CEF’s online portal has closed.
Applicants will be notified of the outcome of their applications within two to three weeks, provided all requested information and references are submitted promptly.
The outcome will be communicated via email.
Supporting documents must be uploaded with the application form.
CEF reserves the right to request further information and documentation.
Evidence of applicant eligibility, a letter of acceptance for the university course, SAAS Award Notice letter, and P60/pay slips/Universal Credit statements are required supporting documents.
Students receiving a SAAS bursary must provide a copy of their SAAS award letter.
Supporting evidence can be submitted as scanned copies or mobile images.
There is a 5MB size limit on each file submitted online.
The scheme supports students who attended university or college in the past but withdrew before completing their studies.
The scheme also helps students seeking asylum in the UK.
Applicants must not have already graduated with a university degree, unless applying for a second undergraduate degree under specific criteria.
For second degree applications, students must have completed their first degree at least two years before the start of their new course.
For second degree applications, students must enter the first year of their course in academic year 2026-27.
For second degree applications, students must have been unable to gain employment in the subject area of their previous degree, be unemployed, have been made redundant or are facing redundancy.

For second degree applications, students must wish to reskill in a different field of study unrelated to their previous qualifications and recognised as being in a skills shortage area for the Scottish economy.

The Carnegie Education Fund recognises that many individuals may have encountered difficulties in gaining employment after an undergraduate degree, have suffered career setbacks, experienced health or personal issues which have forced them to reconsider their career path.
CEF has set aside a budget to fund students who completed an undergraduate degree in the past and wish to start an undergraduate degree in a different field of study in academic year 2026-27.
Applications are processed on a first come first served basis.
CEF will consider applications from students who meet the general eligibility criteria and specific criteria for second degrees.

Eligible undergraduate degree courses for second degrees are listed by subject area (Medicine and health, Social work, IT & Computing, Engineering and architecture, Quantitative sciences, Geosciences, Biosciences, Cultural and creative studies).

CEF will take into account previous qualifications, length of time since previous qualification was obtained, current circumstances of the individual and motivations for returning to university when considering applications.
Students who have already started a 2nd degree before academic year 2026-27 are not eligible to apply.
The awards cover tuition fees only, up to a maximum of £1,820.
Household income thresholds are used as guides, not hard cut-offs, and applications are reviewed holistically.
Gross pay is used for income assessment, before deductions.
Student living cost loan or social benefits are not regarded as part of an applicant’s total household income.
Household income thresholds are provided for single person households and couple households, with variations for the number of children.
CEF may request additional supporting evidence.
The application form is only accessible during the application window.
If an applicant does not receive a confirmation email within 10 minutes, they should contact CEF.
No exceptions or exemptions will be made to any of the eligibility criteria.
The scheme supports students enrolled on an undergraduate degree course at a Scottish Institute of Higher Education.
The scheme supports students who are not eligible for government funding for their tuition fees.
